hints: Focus on the fact that you need to satisfy two separate tests at once, chirality for optical isomerism and a specific group for the iodoform test.
Recall that alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate only with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so first filter out any structures missing both.
Now look for a carbon attached to four different groups in the remaining candidates, that chiral centre is the final link to the answer.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two conditions**

You need both properties in the same molecule. Optical isomerism needs a chiral centre, a carbon with four different groups. The iodoform test needs a methyl ketone or related group.

Positive iodoform group:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ or } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$$

**Apply the iodoform test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine gives $\text{CHI}_3$ (yellow precipitate) with ethanal, methyl ketones and secondary alcohols of the form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. Check each structure for this fragment.

**Check for chirality**

Now test the survivors for a chiral carbon. In $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$, the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{COCH}_3$. That is four different groups, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism, and it also contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ for a positive iodoform test.

options.A: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$ is 3-hydroxybutan-2-one. It contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so gives a positive iodoform test. Its C3, the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon, has four different groups ($\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{COCH}_3$) so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ does contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so it gives a positive iodoform test, but it has no chiral centre. Both middle carbons are $\text{CH}_2$ groups with two identical H atoms, so no optical isomerism.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$ does have a chiral centre at $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)}$ bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{CHO}$, so it shows optical isomerism. However it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ and no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so the iodoform test is negative.
options.D: Incorrect. $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(OH)CHO}$ fails both tests. The central $\text{C(OH)}$ is bonded to two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so it is achiral. It also lacks $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, the $\text{C(OH)}$ is tertiary and cannot be oxidised like a methyl secondary alcohol, so no iodoform reaction.
